    "- 'Which of the following describes a binary search tree?' (definition only, short) → nano\n"
    "- 'Which of the following is true about cache coherence?' → mini\n\n"
    "**Python Easy Router Function:**\n"
    "- route_easy_case(question, options, category='', source='') must return only 'nano', 'mini', or 'defer'.\n"
    "- It may return 'nano' only for very short, obvious definition/abbreviation/fact/code questions with no hard markers.\n"
    "- It must return 'defer' for all other cases, including any question with:\n"
    "  - Negations ('not', 'except', 'none of the above', 'not enough information')\n"
    "  - 'Which of the following' (unless short, direct property/definition)\n"
    "  - Roman numerals ('I.', 'II.', 'III.')\n"
    "  - Advanced topics/markers: 'cache', 'matrix', 'rank', 'unification', 'boolean', 'recurs', 'probability', 'capacity', 'entropy', 'half-life', 'bayesian', 'vertex cover', 'maximum clique', 'maximum flow', 'chord', 'dht', 'nmap', 'protocol', 'graph', 'tree', 'heap', 'stack overflow', 'deadlock', 'critical section', 'mutual exclusion', 'invariant'\n"
    "- Must not use imports, loops, classes, files, or network.\n\n"
    "**Output Requirements:**\n"
    "- Always output exactly one token: nano or mini. No explanation or additional text.\n"
    "- Python code must define route_easy_case as above.\n\n"
    "**Summary:**\n"
    "- Deterministic Python handles only the most obvious easy cases; all others are routed to the LLM for model selection.\n"
    "- Escalate to mini whenever nano is likely to fail but mini is likely to succeed.\n"
    "- Output exactly one token: nano or mini."
)

def route_easy_case(question, options, category="", source=""):
    """Return 'nano' for only the most obvious short definition/abbreviation/fact/code questions with no hard markers; 'defer' otherwise."""
    q = question.strip().lower()
    opt = "\n".join(options).lower()
    text = q + "\n" + opt

    # Escalate to mini for these patterns/topics
    hard_markers = [
        "not", "except", "none of the above", "not enough information",
        "which of the following", "i.", "ii.", "iii.",
        "cache", "matrix", "rank", "unification", "boolean", "recurs", "probability",
        "capacity", "entropy", "half-life", "bayesian", "vertex cover", "maximum clique",
        "maximum flow", "chord", "dht", "nmap", "protocol", "graph", "tree", "heap",
        "stack overflow", "deadlock", "critical section", "mutual exclusion", "invariant"
    ]
    for marker in hard_markers:
        if marker in text:
            return "defer"

    # Allow nano only for very short, direct, obvious cases (definition/abbreviation/expansion/fact)
    easy_markers = [
        "what is", "what are", "define", "definition", "stands for", "expansion of",
        "meaning of", "short for", "full form of", "abbreviation"
    ]
    # Very short, direct questions only (excluding any 'which of the following')
    if (
        len(q) < 100 and
        any(marker in q for marker in easy_markers) and
        "which of the following" not in q
    ):
        return "nano"
    # 'What does X stand for?', 'What is the abbreviation of Y?'
    if (
        len(q) < 100 and
        (
            ("what does" in q and "stand for" in q) or
            ("abbreviation of" in q) or
            ("full form of" in q)
        )
    ):
        return "nano"
    # Allow for trivial code output: single assignment or very tiny for/while (no if, no logic)
    if (
        len(q) < 100 and
        ("output of" in q or "result of" in q or "value of" in q) and
        all(x not in q for x in ["if", "else", "elif", "recurs", "while", "switch", "case", ":"]) and
        any(x in q for x in ["assignment", "=", "print("]) and
        "which of the following" not in q
    ):
        return "nano"

    return "defer"
